body:
I think it's fair to call this an error, since there is no correct behaviour possible without one.

If there were one, then the wording shouldn't be "must", "missing", but advise why you probably want it.
Is a type having a non-public parameterless constructor acceptable?
In my experience, yes.   A non-public (internal, protected, private) parameterless constructor seems to be valid.  I could be wrong though.
